ImageDescription.value:
Carkeek Park picnic grounds, 1922. This would not be Seattle's present-day Carkeek Park: it would be on the site of what is known today as Magnuson Park. The Carkeek Park depicted here (1918–1926) was displaced by the Naval Air Station; it eventually reverted back to the city and became Magnuson Park.

ImageDescription.value: This black and white photograph shows an outdoor market or food court area. There are numerous wooden picnic tables and benches where people are gathered, eating and socializing. In the background, there are vendor stalls or tents set up under some kind of covered area. Tall light poles illuminate the space, and power lines can be seen crossing overhead. The scene has a casual, community atmosphere with trees providing some natural elements around the perimeter. In the distance, there appears to be a hill or mountain formation. The overall setting seems to be a public gathering place, possibly a night market, food festival, or community event where people come together to eat and spend time outdoors. The monochrome treatment gives the photo a timeless, documentary-style quality.
